papers.title: MonoLaDN: Language-Guided DeNoising for Monocular 3D Object Detection
papers.abstract_en: Monocular 3D object detection offers a low-cost route to 3D perception, but it remains fundamentally ill-posed, since depth must be inferred from a single view. Recent transformer-based detectors learn geometry purely from image features and 3D box annotations, lacking the high-level semantic priors that vision-language models (VLMs) acquire from large-scale pretraining. VLMs offer such priors, but deploying one directly as a detector is impractical due to its heavy inference cost. We propose MonoLaDN, a language-guided denoising framework that transfers the geometric reasoning of a VLM into a monocular 3D detector while keeping the deployed model purely vision-based. During training, a frozen VLM produces structured reasoning about each object's occlusion, depth, dimension, and angle from the image and its ground-truth boxes. We encode this reasoning into queries, perturb them with noise, and train the detector to reconstruct the clean reasoning. Reconstructing the corrupted reasoning forces the detector's depth-guided features to internalize the VLM's geometric priors, so this knowledge remains available even after the reasoning path is discarded at inference, adding no latency or parameters to the deployed model. Experiments on KITTI 3D and nuScenes show that MonoLaDN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art detectors and generalizes well to new domains.
papers.abstract_zh: 单目3D目标检测为3D感知提供了一条低成本路径，但由于深度必须从单一视角推断，该问题本质上是不适定的。近期基于Transformer的检测器仅从图像特征和3D框标注中学习几何信息，缺乏视觉语言模型（VLM）从大规模预训练中获得的高层语义先验。VLM可提供此类先验，但因其推理开销大，直接将其部署为检测器并不现实。我们提出MonoLaDN，一种语言引导的去噪框架，将VLM的几何推理能力迁移到单目3D检测器中，同时使部署模型保持纯视觉。训练时，一个冻结的VLM根据图像及其真值框，对每个目标的遮挡、深度、尺寸和角度生成结构化推理。我们将该推理编码为查询，对其施加噪声扰动，并训练检测器重建干净的推理。重建被破坏的推理迫使检测器的深度引导特征内化VLM的几何先验，因此即使在推理阶段丢弃推理路径，这些知识仍然可用，且不为部署模型增加任何延迟或参数。在KITTI 3D和nuScenes上的实验表明，MonoLaDN持续优于最先进的检测器，并能很好地泛化到新领域。
papers.tldr_zh: MonoLaDN在训练时用冻结VLM生成的结构化几何推理经加噪后训练检测器重建，使纯视觉单目3D检测器内化VLM几何先验，推理时无额外开销，在KITTI 3D和nuScenes上优于现有方法。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: PSGAgent: Enhancing MLLMs' Dynamic Visual Perception for Panoptic Scene Graph Generation via Agentic Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Panoptic Scene Graph generation (PSG) requires holistic yet fine-grained reasoning over complex relations among objects. However, current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) applied to PSG suffer from a perception bottleneck: they function as static observers limited by fixed-resolution views. As a result, models often overlook critical relations involving small or peripheral objects and struggle to differentiate ambiguous predicates in complex scenes. To address these limitations, we propose PSGAgent, an agentic framework that enhances visual perception for PSG through a think-act-observe loop. PSGAgent allows MLLMs to dynamically refine their visual perception using two tools: a Region Zoom-In Tool for local exploration of small or boundary relations and a Visual Highlight Tool for relation-focused segmentation that filters out irrelevant contextual noise. To optimize decision-making, we construct a two-stage training pipeline. First, we create a high-quality, error-aware Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (M-CoT) dataset that provides robust supervision for cold-start learning. Then, we design a novel hierarchical reward mechanism integrated with Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) to enable strategic and adaptive tool usage. Extensive experiments on the PSG benchmark show that PSGAgent achieves SOTA performance, demonstrating strong capability in both holistic and fine-grained scene understanding.
papers.abstract_zh: 全景场景图生成（PSG）需要对物体之间复杂关系进行整体而细粒度的推理。然而，当前应用于 PSG 的多模态大语言模型（MLLM）存在感知瓶颈：它们作为静态观察者，受限于固定分辨率的视图。因此，模型常常忽略涉及小型或边缘物体的关键关系，并难以在复杂场景中区分模糊的谓词。为解决这些局限，我们提出 PSGAgent，一个通过“思考—行动—观察”循环增强 PSG 视觉感知的智能体框架。PSGAgent 允许 MLLM 使用两种工具动态细化其视觉感知：用于对小型或边界关系进行局部探索的区域放大工具，以及用于以关系为中心的分割、过滤无关上下文噪声的视觉高亮工具。为优化决策，我们构建了两阶段训练流程。首先，我们创建一个高质量、错误感知的多模态思维链（M-CoT）数据集，为冷启动学习提供稳健监督。然后，我们设计一种新颖的分层奖励机制，并与组序列策略优化（GSPO）结合，以实现策略性和自适应的工具使用。在 PSG 基准上的大量实验表明，PSGAgent 达到 SOTA 性能，展现出在整体和细粒度场景理解方面的强大能力。
papers.tldr_zh: PSGAgent 通过“思考—行动—观察”循环与区域放大、视觉高亮两种工具，结合两阶段训练和分层奖励机制，提升 MLLM 在全景场景图生成中的动态视觉感知，并在 PSG 基准上达到 SOTA。

匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model

papers.title: Amortized Nonlinear Variable Selection with Prior-Data Fitted Networks
papers.abstract_en: Variable selection is an important task for interpreting potentially complex systems in fields such as biology, business, and sociology. The importance of variable selection has attracted considerable attention in statistics and machine learning. In this paper, we are mainly interested in model-agnostic variable selection for identifying variables that have general nonlinear dependence on the response. We propose MambaPFN, short for Model-Agnostic Markov BlAnket selection with Prior-data Fitted Networks, which is built upon the Transformer, a building block of many popular large language models. Specifically, we consider a functional-mapping perspective on variable-selection learning, in which the Transformer is treated as a learnable mapping from a dataset to its relevant variables. To learn this mapping, MambaPFN introduces three new components: (i) a faithful, rich, and scalable scheme for generating pretraining data, (ii) an objective that targets each variable's posterior inclusion probability, and (iii) a modified Transformer architecture tailored to variable selection. Once pretrained, MambaPFN is applied to new datasets without parameter updates. Empirically, MambaPFN achieves desirable variable-selection performance in simulation studies and exhibits a scaling law---more pretraining datasets and larger models can continuously improve its performance. Applied to a Facebook comments dataset, MambaPFN selects the fewest variables and achieves the highest computational efficiency and predictive performance, improving upon the best baselines by about 20%.
papers.abstract_zh: 变量选择是解释生物学、商业和社会学等领域中潜在复杂系统的一项重要任务。变量选择的重要性在统计学和机器学习领域引起了广泛关注。本文主要关注模型无关的变量选择，用于识别与响应变量具有一般非线性依赖关系的变量。我们提出 MambaPFN，即基于先验数据拟合网络的模型无关马尔可夫毯选择（Model-Agnostic Markov BlAnket selection with Prior-data Fitted Networks），它建立在 Transformer 之上，而 Transformer 是许多流行大语言模型的基本构件。具体而言，我们从函数映射的视角看待变量选择学习，将 Transformer 视为从数据集到其相关变量的可学习映射。为学习这一映射，MambaPFN 引入了三个新组件：（i）一种忠实、丰富且可扩展的预训练数据生成方案，（ii）一个以每个变量的后验包含概率为目标的目标函数，以及（iii）一种为变量选择量身定制的改进 Transformer 架构。预训练后，MambaPFN 无需参数更新即可应用于新数据集。在实证上，MambaPFN 在模拟研究中取得了理想的变量选择性能，并展现出缩放规律——更多预训练数据集和更大模型可以持续提升其性能。应用于 Facebook 评论数据集时，MambaPFN 选择的变量最少，并实现了最高的计算效率和预测性能，较最佳基线提升约 20%。
papers.tldr_zh: MambaPFN 将 Transformer 视为从数据集到相关变量的可学习映射，通过预训练数据生成、后验包含概率目标和改进架构实现无需参数更新的模型无关非线性变量选择，并在 Facebook 评论数据集上以最少变量取得最高效率与预测性能。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model, transformer
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining
匹配 模型架构：transformer architecture

papers.title: DSRS: Teaching MLLMs to Perceive, Reason, and Segment in Complex Driving Scenes
papers.abstract_en: Existing reasoning segmentation frameworks typically employ multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with broad world knowledge to extract semantics in a human-like manner and generate corresponding segmentation masks. Nevertheless, these frameworks lack the necessary scene-specific awareness. This paper introduces driving scene reasoning segmentation (DSRS), a scene-specific task that requires models to interpret implicit instructions, infer spatial relations, detect potential risks, handle challenging conditions, and comprehend underlying traffic rules, ultimately generating accurate segmentation masks. Meanwhile, we establish a benchmark dataset to facilitate future research on the DSRS task. To pioneer this task, we propose DSRS-Net, a novel architecture with advanced reasoning segmentation capability for automated driving. Specifically, DSRS-Net seamlessly infuses geometric features for deeper reasoning segmentation, without compromising the original multimodal fusion mechanism. This strategy effectively mitigates the modality representation mismatch in MLLMs caused by RGB-only pretraining, while enhancing the integration of geometric, contextual, and linguistic features. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance of DSRS-Net in both driving scene reasoning segmentation and other language-driven segmentation tasks across various public datasets. The source code and dataset will be released upon publication.
papers.abstract_zh: 现有的推理分割框架通常采用具备广泛世界知识的多模态大语言模型（MLLM），以类人的方式提取语义并生成相应的分割掩码。然而，这些框架缺乏必要的场景特定感知能力。本文提出驾驶场景推理分割（DSRS），这是一个场景特定任务，要求模型解读隐式指令、推断空间关系、检测潜在风险、处理挑战性条件并理解底层交通规则，最终生成准确的分割掩码。同时，我们建立了一个基准数据集以促进DSRS任务的未来研究。为开创该任务，我们提出DSRS-Net，一种面向自动驾驶、具备先进推理分割能力的新架构。具体而言，DSRS-Net在不损害原有多模态融合机制的前提下，无缝注入几何特征以实现更深入的推理分割。该策略有效缓解了MLLM因仅RGB预训练导致的模态表示不匹配，同时增强了几何、上下文和语言特征的整合。大量实验表明，DSRS-Net在驾驶场景推理分割及多个公开数据集上的其他语言驱动分割任务中均表现优异。源代码和数据集将在论文发表后发布。
papers.tldr_zh: 论文提出驾驶场景推理分割任务DSRS并构建基准数据集，提出DSRS-Net在保持多模态融合机制的同时注入几何特征，缓解RGB预训练导致的模态表示不匹配，在驾驶场景推理分割等任务上表现优异。

papers.title: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) enables multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to scale capacity efficiently, but expert parameters dominate memory even though only a few experts are activated per token: they account for over 90% of model size in modern MoE-MLLMs (e.g., 54 GB out of about 58 GB in BF16 for InternVL3.5-30B-A3B and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B). Expert pruning has emerged as an effective compression strategy, but existing methods aggregate importance uniformly across tokens, ignoring that the same expert may serve different roles for vision versus language processing. To address this, we propose MAEP (Modality-Aware Expert Pruning), a training-free framework that decomposes expert importance by modality in a single forward pass. MAEP introduces (1) Delta-H Output ($ΔH$), a redistribution-aware metric measuring the MoE output change when an expert is removed, and (2) low-attention vision tokens as a vision-side pruning signal that is dataset-stable: its expert-importance ranking remains stable across different datasets. Text-side importance serves as a preservation signal while vision-side importance serves as a pruning signal, and experts are ranked globally across layers. Experiments on three MoE-based MLLMs across multimodal and text benchmarks show that MAEP outperforms modality-agnostic baselines on the majority of multimodal benchmarks while remaining competitive on text-only tasks, reducing the BF16 expert weight footprint by about 27 GB (about 47% of total memory) so that the full weight footprint of an approximately 58 GB model fits within a single 40 GB GPU. Code is available at https://github.com/nota-github/MAEP.
papers.abstract_zh: 混合专家（MoE）使多模态大语言模型（MLLM）能够高效扩展容量，但专家参数主导内存占用，尽管每个token仅激活少数专家：在现代MoE-MLLM中，专家参数占模型规模的90%以上（例如InternVL3.5-30B-A3B和Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B在BF16下约58 GB中的54 GB）。专家剪枝已成为一种有效的压缩策略，但现有方法在所有token上统一聚合重要性，忽略了同一专家在视觉与语言处理中可能承担不同角色。为此，我们提出MAEP（模态感知专家剪枝），一个无需训练的框架，在单次前向传播中按模态分解专家重要性。MAEP引入（1）Delta-H输出（ΔH），一种衡量移除某专家时MoE输出变化的再分配感知指标，以及（2）低注意力视觉token作为视觉侧剪枝信号，该信号具有数据集稳定性：其专家重要性排序在不同数据集间保持稳定。文本侧重要性作为保留信号，视觉侧重要性作为剪枝信号，专家在跨层范围内全局排序。在三个MoE-MLLM上跨多模态和文本基准的实验表明，MAEP在多数多模态基准上优于模态无关基线，同时在纯文本任务上保持竞争力，将BF16专家权重占用减少约27 GB（约占总内存的47%），使约58 GB模型的全部权重可装入单张40 GB GPU。代码见https://github.com/nota-github/MAEP。
papers.tldr_zh: MAEP按模态分解专家重要性，以视觉侧低注意力token为剪枝信号、文本侧为保留信号并跨层全局排序，无需训练即可将MoE-MLLM专家权重减少约27 GB，多模态基准上优于模态无关基线。

匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model

papers.title: ProQuant: Progressive Quantization-aware Training for Edge MLLMs
papers.abstract_en: Multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) with impressive perception and understanding capabilities will enable a range of downstream applications. However, their substantial computational and memory requirements hinder the real-world implementation, particularly for resource-constrained edge devices. Quantization has emerged as an effective solution for deploying large models. While post-training quantization (PTQ) successfully retains the performance at moderate bit-width (e.g., W8A8), it suffers from severe performance degradation under low-bit quantization (e.g., W4A8), especially for small-scale models that are more suitable for edge deployment. In this paper, we propose ProQuant, a novel weight-activation quantization-aware training (QAT) framework tailored for low-bit MLLMs. First, to align the limited finetuning dataset distribution with the pretrained dataset distribution, we propose a self-relabeling (SRL) scheme to resample the responses of the open-source multimodal dataset. Second, we are the first to take a decoupled view of multi-modal (MM) understanding and language modeling abilities. We propose a progressive block activation (PBA) mechanism to prioritize the MM understanding recovery. We also introduce a vision-sensitive factor $\vecτ$ that effectively identifies the MM-critical layers. Extensive experiments across various benchmarks, covering models with 2B-8B parameters, show that ProQuant significantly outperforms existing methods. For example, our W4A8 Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct improves average accuracy by impressively 6.6% and achieves performance comparable to full precision counterparts with only approximately 1% performance drop. Code is available at https://github.com/yufeixue-ai/ProQuant/.
papers.abstract_zh: 具有出色感知与理解能力的多模态大语言模型（MLLM）将支持一系列下游应用。然而，其巨大的计算和内存需求阻碍了实际部署，尤其是在资源受限的边缘设备上。量化已成为部署大模型的有效方案。训练后量化（PTQ）在中等位宽（如 W8A8）下成功保持性能，但在低位量化（如 W4A8）下性能严重下降，对于更适合边缘部署的小规模模型尤其如此。本文提出 ProQuant，一种面向低位 MLLM 的新型权重—激活量化感知训练（QAT）框架。首先，为使有限的微调数据集分布与预训练数据集分布对齐，我们提出自重新标注（SRL）方案，对开源多模态数据集的响应进行重采样。其次，我们首次从解耦视角看待多模态（MM）理解与语言建模能力。我们提出渐进式块激活（PBA）机制，以优先恢复 MM 理解能力。我们还引入视觉敏感因子 $\vecτ$，有效识别 MM 关键层。跨多种基准、覆盖 2B–8B 参数模型的大量实验表明，ProQuant 显著优于现有方法。例如，我们的 W4A8 Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct 将平均准确率显著提升 6.6%，仅约 1% 的性能下降即达到与全精度对应模型相当的性能。代码见 https://github.com/yufeixue-ai/ProQuant/。
papers.tldr_zh: ProQuant 提出面向低位 MLLM 的权重—激活量化感知训练框架，通过自重新标注、渐进式块激活和视觉敏感因子优先恢复多模态理解能力，在 2B–8B 模型上显著优于现有方法。

papers.title: Entropogram-guided Visual Realignment Decoding: Capturing the Rhythm of Multimodal Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable progress on cross-modal reasoning tasks, yet they continue to suffer from hallucinations in long-chain reasoning processes. In this work, we revisit hallucination in MLLMs from the perspective of reasoning generation dynamics. We argue that entropy is not merely a static measure of uncertainty but a structured signal that reflects how modality information is integrated throughout decoding. Through systematic analysis, we identify two characteristic entropy patterns associated with hallucination behaviors: (1) a generally high-confidence regime corresponds to premature convergence to inappropriate multimodal interactions; and (2) local abrupt entropy transitions are associated with reasoning instability and hallucination onset. Building on these observations, we propose an entropy-aware self-introspective framework for MLLM reasoning. Our method continuously tracks entropy dynamics during decoding and performs targeted visual re-alignment when suspicious hallucination states are detected, encouraging the model to re-examine salient visual evidence at critical reasoning stages. Extensive experiments across six multimodal reasoning benchmarks spanning nine distinct evaluation settings demonstrate that our approach delivers robust improvements in reasoning accuracy and hallucination robustness, while providing new insights into the generation dynamics underlying MLLM failures. The code is available at: https://github.com/jden4524/SelfRetrospectiveDecoding.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型（MLLM）在跨模态推理任务上取得了显著进展，但在长链推理过程中仍存在幻觉问题。本文从推理生成动态的视角重新审视MLLM中的幻觉。我们认为熵不仅是静态的不确定性度量，更是反映模态信息在整个解码过程中如何整合的结构化信号。通过系统分析，我们识别出与幻觉行为相关的两种特征性熵模式：（1）整体高置信度状态对应于过早收敛到不恰当的多模态交互；（2）局部熵的突变与推理不稳定和幻觉发生相关。基于这些观察，我们提出一种面向MLLM推理的熵感知自省框架。该方法在解码过程中持续跟踪熵动态，并在检测到可疑幻觉状态时执行有针对性的视觉重对齐，促使模型在关键推理阶段重新审视显著视觉证据。在涵盖九种不同评估设置的六个多模态推理基准上的大量实验表明，该方法在推理准确性和幻觉鲁棒性上均带来稳健提升，同时为MLLM失败的生成动态提供了新见解。代码见：https://github.com/jden4524/SelfRetrospectiveDecoding。
papers.tldr_zh: 论文从解码熵动态视角分析MLLM幻觉，识别出高置信度过早收敛与局部熵突变两种模式，提出熵感知自省框架在检测到可疑状态时进行视觉重对齐，在六个多模态推理基准上提升准确性与幻觉鲁棒性。

papers.title: Pixel-space video generation with U-JiT
papers.abstract_en: Latent diffusion and flow matching models are ubiquitous in state-of-the-art generative video models. While highly effective, relying on pretrained autoencoders to compress the data into a lower-dimensional latent space also comes with drawbacks. First, training proceeds in two stages: autoencoder pretraining, with compression and reconstruction objectives, followed by latent generative model training, precluding fully end-to-end training. Second, autoencoders also lead to an inherent loss of signal, and the trade-off between reconstruction quality and generative performance in the latent space is still an active area of research. In this paper we explore the viability of generative video models directly in pixel space. We analyze recent approaches in pixel-space generative modeling of images that rely on basic transformer designs, and identify several shortcomings that limit their effectiveness for the high-dimensional pixel-space video generation. To overcome these limitations, we propose a UNet-like transformer architecture along with improvements to the training recipe and sampling strategy. We conduct controlled experiments, training latent and pixel-space models from scratch on Kinetics-600. For the standard frames-to-video task at 128 resolution, our U-JiT model improves generative FVD by 27% over prior state-of-the-art results, and by 14% against the JiT pixel-space baseline. Scaling to higher 256 resolution, we find the improvement over pixel-space and latent-based models grows as we increase the spatiotemporal compression rate up to $64 \times 64 \times 8$. Finally, we find that U-JiT improves per-frame FID by 27% over latent models and 61% over pixel-space models on class-to-video generation, with respectively 9% and 56% reduction in FVD.
papers.abstract_zh: 潜空间扩散与流匹配模型在当前最先进的生成式视频模型中无处不在。尽管非常有效，依赖预训练自编码器将数据压缩到低维潜空间也带来了缺点。首先，训练分两个阶段进行：先以压缩和重建为目标预训练自编码器，再训练潜空间生成模型，这排除了完全端到端训练的可能。其次，自编码器还会导致固有的信号损失，而潜空间中重建质量与生成性能之间的权衡仍是活跃的研究领域。本文探索直接在像素空间构建生成式视频模型的可行性。我们分析了近期依赖基础 Transformer 设计的图像像素空间生成建模方法，并指出若干限制其在高维像素空间视频生成中有效性的缺陷。为克服这些限制，我们提出一种类 UNet 的 Transformer 架构，并改进训练配方与采样策略。我们在 Kinetics-600 上从头训练潜空间与像素空间模型，进行受控实验。对于 128 分辨率下的标准帧到视频任务，我们的 U-JiT 模型将生成 FVD 较此前最先进结果提升 27%，较 JiT 像素空间基线提升 14%。扩展到更高的 256 分辨率时，我们发现随着时空压缩率提高到 $64 \times 64 \times 8$，相对像素空间和基于潜空间的模型的改进随之增大。最后，我们发现 U-JiT 在类别到视频生成上将逐帧 FID 较潜空间模型提升 27%、较像素空间模型提升 61%，FVD 分别降低 9% 和 56%。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出类 UNet 的 Transformer 架构 U-JiT 直接在像素空间生成视频，并在 Kinetics-600 上较像素空间与潜空间基线取得更优的 FVD 和 FID。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining
匹配 模型架构：transformer architecture
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Open-HumanWAM: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
papers.abstract_en: Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes. We introduce Open-HumanWAM, the first fully open recipe for scaling egocentric pretraining to 50,000 hours, anchored by Open-HumanWAM-50K---a curated egocentric video corpus densely annotated with hand motion and natural language. Leveraging this corpus, we systematically investigate pure human pretraining via closed-loop simulation evaluations and uncover an empirical log-linear scaling law linking pretraining data hours to downstream robot success rates. Grounded in these findings, we develop HumanWAM-Vanilla, a world--action model pretrained exclusively on 50k hours of egocentric human video. Upon robot post-training, HumanWAM-Vanilla reaches 92.08% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean and 68.88% on Clean2Random, alongside a 14.17% mean success rate and a 19.00 mean progress score on RoboDojo. To push the capability frontier further, we explore joint human--robot pretraining with HumanWAM-Goal, a visual-goal-conditioned world--action model. Hybrid data scaling unlocks broad zero-shot generalization across both simulation and physical benchmarks, propelling post-trained RoboTwin 2.0 performance to new state-of-the-art levels: 92.70% on Clean2Clean and a substantial leap to 84.60% on Clean2Random. On physical robots, HumanWAM-Goal further exhibits emergent embodied in-context learning, dynamically adapting its manipulation behavior to unseen visual goals without parameter updates. To support reproducible scaling research in embodied AI, we open-source the Open-HumanWAM-50K corpus, data curation and pretraining pipelines, alongside the pretrained and post-trained HumanWAM checkpoints, inference code, and simulation evaluation suites.
papers.abstract_zh: 第一人称人类视频为机器人学习提供了可扩展的操作先验来源，但将原始数据规模转化为可泛化的机器人策略需要严格的数据整理与训练配方。我们提出 Open-HumanWAM，首个将第一人称预训练扩展至 50,000 小时的完全开放配方，其核心是 Open-HumanWAM-50K——一个经整理、密集标注手部运动和自然语言的第一人称视频语料库。利用该语料库，我们通过闭环仿真评估系统研究纯人类预训练，并发现将预训练数据小时数与下游机器人成功率联系起来的经验对数线性缩放定律。基于这些发现，我们开发 HumanWAM-Vanilla，一个仅用 50k 小时第一人称人类视频预训练的世界—动作模型。经机器人后训练后，HumanWAM-Vanilla 在 RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean 上达到 92.08% 成功率，在 Clean2Random 上达到 68.88%，并在 RoboDojo 上取得 14.17% 平均成功率和 19.00 平均进度分数。为进一步推进能力前沿，我们探索人—机器人联合预训练，提出 HumanWAM-Goal，一个视觉目标条件世界—动作模型。混合数据缩放解锁了跨仿真和物理基准的广泛零样本泛化，将后训练的 RoboTwin 2.0 性能推至新的 SOTA 水平：Clean2Clean 上 92.70%，Clean2Random 上大幅跃升至 84.60%。在物理机器人上，HumanWAM-Goal 进一步展现出涌现的具身上下文学习能力，无需参数更新即可动态调整其操作行为以适应未见过的视觉目标。为支持具身 AI 中可复现的缩放研究，我们开源 Open-HumanWAM-50K 语料库、数据整理与预训练流程，以及预训练和后训练的 HumanWAM 检查点、推理代码和仿真评估套件。
papers.tldr_zh: Open-HumanWAM 提出首个将第一人称人类视频预训练扩展至 50,000 小时的开放配方，发现数据小时数与机器人成功率的对数线性缩放定律，并通过纯人类预训练和联合预训练模型在 RoboTwin 2.0 等基准上取得 SOTA 或涌现的零样本泛化能力。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining, post-training
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: ModalSearcher: Weaving Visual Evidence into Autonomous Cross-Modal Deep Search
papers.abstract_en: Static and incomplete parametric knowledge limits the performance of multimodal large language models on novel-knowledge and knowledge-intensive tasks, especially those requiring multi-hop evidence acquisition. Existing multimodal agentic search methods often fix visual evidence at the input or a predefined trajectory position, making it difficult for agents to select search modalities as their information needs evolve and to handle complex real-world queries. We define this capability as autonomous cross-modal search: an agent chooses among direct reasoning, text-to-text search, text-to-image search, and reverse-image search, actively introduces visual evidence when appropriate, and switches between and integrates modalities across multiple hops. We propose ModalSearch-Pipeline, a scalable procedure for constructing an interleaved multimodal knowledge graph. It samples paths with diverse depths and modality compositions and uses backward question construction to obscure entity names and image targets that would expose reasoning shortcuts while retaining necessary disambiguating clues, yielding text-only, image-initialized, and arbitrarily interleaved multi-hop problems. We train the ModalSearcher Agent with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning in a live Web environment, and construct ModalSearch-Bench. Experiments show that ModalSearcher-8B improves average accuracy by 16.2 points over Qwen3-VL-8B under the same agentic workflow across five multimodal knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks, with consistent gains on independently constructed active visual-search benchmarks.
papers.abstract_zh: 静态且不完整的参数化知识限制了多模态大语言模型在新知识和知识密集型任务上的表现，尤其是那些需要多跳证据获取的任务。现有多模态智能体搜索方法通常将视觉证据固定在输入或预定义的轨迹位置，使智能体难以随着信息需求的变化选择搜索模态，也难以处理复杂的现实世界查询。我们将这一能力定义为自主跨模态搜索：智能体在直接推理、文本到文本搜索、文本到图像搜索和反向图像搜索之间进行选择，在适当时主动引入视觉证据，并在多跳过程中切换和整合模态。我们提出 ModalSearch-Pipeline，一种用于构建交错多模态知识图谱的可扩展流程。它采样具有多样深度和模态组成的路径，并使用反向问题构建来遮蔽会暴露推理捷径的实体名称和图像目标，同时保留必要的消歧线索，从而生成纯文本、图像初始化和任意交错的多跳问题。我们在实时 Web 环境中通过监督微调和强化学习训练 ModalSearcher Agent，并构建了 ModalSearch-Bench。实验表明，在相同的智能体工作流下，ModalSearcher-8B 在五个多模态知识密集型问答基准上相较 Qwen3-VL-8B 平均准确率提升 16.2 个百分点，并在独立构建的主动视觉搜索基准上取得一致增益。
papers.tldr_zh: 定义自主跨模态搜索能力并提出 ModalSearch-Pipeline 构建交错多模态知识图谱，训练 ModalSearcher-8B 智能体，在五个多模态知识密集型问答基准上较 Qwen3-VL-8B 平均准确率提升 16.2 个百分点。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Do Agentic Policies Need to Look at Every Step? Geometric Abstraction for Reasoning and Action
papers.abstract_en: Recent multimodal language models can reason directly about robot scenes, but it is unclear whether they need to repeatedly reinterpret raw visual observations at every step of an interaction. We propose shifting routine spatial reasoning from images to text and symbols through a 3D geometric abstraction that is refreshed locally from observations and read directly by the language models. Specifically, our interface represents scene geometry via typed, evidence-aware symbolic references to object parts, grounds them from calibrated RGB-D, and returns compact textual checkpoints with metric residuals after each action. Symbolic task structure can thus be reused across decisions while metric values are rebound to the current scene, with direct visual reasoning invoked only on demand. Across offline policy synthesis and continuous online execution, reasoning over grounded text and symbols improves multi-step manipulation completion while substantially reducing repeated multimodal queries, positioning explicit geometric state as an effective substrate for agentic robot policies.
papers.abstract_zh: 近期多模态语言模型可以直接对机器人场景进行推理，但尚不清楚它们是否需要在交互的每一步反复重新解读原始视觉观测。我们提出通过一种 3D 几何抽象，将常规空间推理从图像转移到文本和符号，该抽象从观测中局部刷新并由语言模型直接读取。具体而言，我们的接口通过带类型、证据感知的物体部件符号引用来表示场景几何，从标定 RGB-D 中将其接地，并在每次动作后返回带度量残差的紧凑文本检查点。符号任务结构因而可在决策间复用，而度量值重新绑定到当前场景，仅在需要时调用直接视觉推理。在离线策略合成与连续在线执行中，基于接地的文本和符号进行推理提升了多步操作完成率，同时大幅减少重复的多模态查询，表明显式几何状态是智能体机器人策略的有效基础。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出以 3D 几何抽象将空间推理从图像转为文本符号的接口，在减少重复多模态查询的同时提升多步机器人操作完成率。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal language model
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Equivariant Deep Learning in Direct-Product Space for Electronic-Structure Hamiltonian Prediction
papers.abstract_en: Most existing equivariant architectures for Hamiltonian prediction propagate features in direct-sum spaces of irreducible spherical tensors, whereas the target Hamiltonian is naturally an operator block in a direct-product representation over local orbital and spin bases. This representation mismatch fragments contiguous Hamiltonian blocks, obscures direct manipulation of orbital couplings, and organizes features into irregular angular-momentum components that require numerous transformations and are poorly aligned with efficient hardware execution and memory management. To address both the representation mismatch and computational bottleneck, we propose DP-Learner, an equivariant learning framework that performs message passing directly on Hamiltonian-like operator blocks in the direct-product space. Theoretically, we propose Lie-generator-based directional embedding and invariantly weighted left--right products and contractions that preserve equivariance to SO(3), SU(2), and spatial inversions, without explicit Clebsch--Gordan decomposition or inverse reconstruction. Methodologically, we instantiate this principle as a Transformer architecture, in which Hamiltonian-like feature matrices or tensors evolve through equivariant operators in the direct-product space, while non-linear invariant scalar routing controls structured gating over matrix units, directional propagation, attention, and environment-embedded context interactions. We further construct MP-HAM-110K, a large-scale Hamiltonian dataset comprising more than 110,000 material structures covering 68 elements with both Hamiltonian and wavefunction data. Experiments on MP-HAM-110K and Materials-HAM-SOC demonstrate that DP-Learner dramatically improves Hamiltonian prediction accuracy and inference efficiency over the state-of-the-art method.
papers.abstract_zh: 现有大多数用于哈密顿量预测的等变架构在不可约球张量的直和空间中传播特征，而目标哈密顿量本质上是局部轨道与自旋基上直积表示中的算符块。这种表示不匹配会割裂连续的哈密顿量块，妨碍对轨道耦合的直接操作，并将特征组织为不规则角动量分量，需要大量变换且与高效硬件执行和内存管理对齐不佳。为解决表示不匹配和计算瓶颈，我们提出 DP-Learner，一个直接在直积空间中类哈密顿量算符块上进行消息传递的等变学习框架。理论上，我们提出基于李生成元的定向嵌入以及不变加权的左右乘积与收缩，在无需显式 Clebsch–Gordan 分解或逆重构的情况下保持对 SO(3)、SU(2) 和空间反演的等变性。方法上，我们将该原理实例化为 Transformer 架构，其中类哈密顿量特征矩阵或张量通过直积空间中的等变算符演化，而非线性不变标量路由控制对矩阵单元、定向传播、注意力和环境嵌入上下文交互的结构化门控。我们进一步构建 MP-HAM-110K，一个大规模哈密顿量数据集，包含超过 110,000 个材料结构，覆盖 68 种元素，并同时提供哈密顿量和波函数数据。在 MP-HAM-110K 和 Materials-HAM-SOC 上的实验表明，DP-Learner 相比 SOTA 方法大幅提升了哈密顿量预测准确率和推理效率。
papers.tldr_zh: DP-Learner 在直积空间中直接对类哈密顿量算符块进行等变消息传递，避免 Clebsch–Gordan 分解并保持 SO(3)、SU(2) 和空间反演等变性，在 MP-HAM-110K 等数据集上显著提升哈密顿量预测准确率与推理效率。
why_it_matters: 匹配 模型架构：transformer architecture
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels
papers.abstract_en: Efficient deployment of large language models (LLMs) on mobile devices requires balancing performance with compute and memory constraints. Post-training compression is an effective approach to managing this trade-off, while requiring much less computation than in-training counterparts. We propose DictLLM, a dictionary-based compression scheme in which weight matrices within grouped layers are decomposed into a shared dictionary and layer-specific sparse coefficients, directly obtained from a pre-trained model without further training. Specifically, we cast DictLLM as a four-step post-training optimization. First, we obtain shared dictionaries via singular value decomposition (SVD) of input-scaled weight matrices, amortizing rank across grouped layers; second, we sparsify the layer-specific coefficients to the target compression ratio using a dictionary-aware Hessian; and third, we refine the dictionaries given the resulting sparse coefficients. Finally, we aggressively quantize both components using factor-specific Hessian information: input covariance for the dictionaries and the dictionary-aware Hessian for the coefficients. The resulting representation reduces memory footprint by storing a single shared dictionary per layer group, along with sparse layer-specific coefficients. On language modeling and zero-shot reasoning benchmarks, DictLLM consistently outperforms existing post-training low-rank compression methods and pushes the Pareto frontier between model size and performance. DictLLM compresses the original LLaMA-7B model by 5.1x with only a 2.9-point increase in WikiText-2 perplexity, achieving a 3.6x higher compression ratio than the state-of-the-art low-rank method.
papers.abstract_zh: 在移动设备上高效部署大语言模型（LLM）需要在性能与计算、内存约束之间取得平衡。训练后压缩是管理这一权衡的有效方法，且所需计算远少于训练中压缩。我们提出 DictLLM，一种基于字典的压缩方案，将分组层内的权重矩阵分解为共享字典和层特定稀疏系数，直接从预训练模型获得而无需进一步训练。具体而言，我们将 DictLLM 表述为四步训练后优化。首先，通过对输入缩放后的权重矩阵进行奇异值分解（SVD）获得共享字典，在分组层间分摊秩；其次，使用字典感知 Hessian 将层特定系数稀疏化至目标压缩率；第三，根据所得稀疏系数细化字典。最后，我们使用因子特定 Hessian 信息对两个分量进行激进量化：字典使用输入协方差，系数使用字典感知 Hessian。所得表示通过为每个层组存储单个共享字典以及稀疏的层特定系数来减少内存占用。在语言建模和零样本推理基准上，DictLLM 持续优于现有训练后低秩压缩方法，并推进模型大小与性能之间的帕累托前沿。DictLLM 将原始 LLaMA-7B 模型压缩 5.1 倍，WikiText-2 困惑度仅增加 2.9 点，压缩率比 SOTA 低秩方法高 3.6 倍。
papers.tldr_zh: DictLLM 将分组层权重矩阵分解为共享字典与层特定稀疏系数，并通过 SVD、字典感知 Hessian 稀疏化、字典细化和因子特定量化四步训练后优化实现压缩，在 LLaMA-7B 上以 5.1 倍压缩仅使 WikiText-2 困惑度增加 2.9 点。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: TSFM Meets LLM: Context as Covariates
papers.abstract_en: Textual information is ubiquitous in real-world time series datasets, appearing as news, reports, and annotations that hold key predictive signals not deducible from numerical history alone. Large Language Models (LLMs) interpret text but lack numerical precision, while Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) are quantitatively accurate but cannot reason about the effects of text. Moreover, the lack of large-scale paired multimodal datasets limits progress in bridging this gap. In this work, we address this challenge by providing a scalable approach for generating realistic multimodal datasets by annotating real-world time series with LLMs. Building on this, we propose Context as Covariates (CoCo), a forecasting framework in which an LLM distills its textual reasoning into numerically grounded forecast and confidence covariates that guide a TSFM backbone, thereby exploiting the strengths of both LLMs and TSFMs. We align the two models in stages, first fine-tuning the LLM via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a reward tied to covariate-induced improvement in forecasting performance, and then fine-tuning the TSFM on covariates generated by the aligned LLM. Our experiments show that models trained on our synthetic multimodal corpus generalize to real benchmarks spanning finance, economics, weather, traffic, and security. Notably, CoCo with Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 as the LLM and Chronos2 as the TSFM achieves up to 12% MAE improvement over state-of-the-art TSFMs and LLM forecasters, such as GPT-4o. Code, checkpoints, and the evaluation datasets are publicly available.
papers.abstract_zh: 文本信息在现实世界的时间序列数据集中无处不在，以新闻、报告和注释的形式出现，其中包含仅凭数值历史无法推断的关键预测信号。大语言模型（LLM）能够解读文本，但缺乏数值精度；时间序列基础模型（TSFM）在定量上准确，但无法推理文本的影响。此外，缺乏大规模配对多模态数据集限制了弥合这一差距的进展。在本工作中，我们通过提供一种可扩展的方法来应对这一挑战：用LLM对现实世界时间序列进行标注，从而生成逼真的多模态数据集。在此基础上，我们提出Context as Covariates（CoCo），一种预测框架，其中LLM将其文本推理蒸馏为有数值依据的预测协变量和置信度协变量，用以引导TSFM主干，从而发挥LLM和TSFM两者的优势。我们分阶段对齐两个模型：首先通过Group Relative Policy Optimization（GRPO）微调LLM，其奖励与协变量带来的预测性能提升挂钩；然后在由对齐后LLM生成的协变量上微调TSFM。我们的实验表明，在我们的合成多模态语料上训练的模型能够泛化到涵盖金融、经济、天气、交通和安全的真实基准。值得注意的是，以Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507作为LLM、Chronos2作为TSFM的CoCo，相比最先进的TSFM和LLM预测器（如GPT-4o）实现了最高12%的MAE改进。代码、检查点和评估数据集已公开。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出CoCo框架，用LLM将文本推理蒸馏为预测与置信度协变量来引导TSFM，并通过GRPO分阶段对齐两模型，在多个真实基准上相比最先进TSFM和GPT-4o等预测器实现最高12%的MAE改进。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model, foundation model
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Analysis of Local Open-Weight LLM Agents on Vulnerability-Reproduction Tasks
papers.abstract_en: Open-weight language models that fit on a single consumer GPU are becoming capable on a growing range of tasks, and they matter because they can run locally without sending the code to a hosted service. Vulnerability reproduction, turning a vulnerability description into an input that crashes the vulnerable build, is a natural target for them, since it is an automated analysis task closer to test generation than to code comprehension and it runs against a build that must be executed rather than read. In order to assess whether current models can perform it, we evaluate twelve configurations of local models, spanning three generations, two architectures and three quantization levels, on ten CyberGym vulnerability-reproduction tasks, three runs each under one harness, and release the full artefact. We show that every configuration, down to the 4B model, solves most of the six easier tasks, and configurations separate only on the remaining four. For the harder tasks, the 27B model is required. Quantization did not change what the models solved in any matched pair, but it changed how fast they got there, and the mixture of experts reached the same scores in less wall clock. We also examine the agent trajectories. Almost every run we examined, including those that fail, names the vulnerable function and states the correct hypothesis, and what separates a solved task from an unsolved one is whether that hypothesis becomes a working input.
papers.abstract_zh: 能够装入单块消费级GPU的开放权重语言模型在越来越多的任务上变得有能力，它们之所以重要，是因为可以在本地运行而无需将代码发送到托管服务。漏洞复现——将漏洞描述转化为能使存在漏洞的构建崩溃的输入——是它们的一个自然目标，因为这是一项自动化分析任务，更接近测试生成而非代码理解，并且它针对的是必须执行而非阅读的构建。为了评估当前模型能否执行该任务，我们在十个CyberGym漏洞复现任务上评估了十二种本地模型配置，涵盖三代、两种架构和三种量化级别，每种配置在同一测试框架下运行三次，并发布完整工件。我们表明，每种配置（直至4B模型）都能解决六个较简单任务中的大多数，配置之间仅在剩余四个任务上出现分化。对于较难的任务，需要27B模型。在任何匹配对中，量化都没有改变模型所解决的任务，但改变了它们达到结果的速度，且混合专家模型以更少的实际耗时达到相同分数。我们还检查了智能体轨迹。我们检查的几乎每次运行（包括失败的运行）都指出了存在漏洞的函数并陈述了正确假设，而解决任务与未解决任务之间的区别在于该假设是否转化为可工作的输入。

papers.title: Decouple to Reuse: Fine-Grained Knowledge Augmentation for Time Series Foundation Models
papers.abstract_en: Time series forecasting is critical for demand prediction and resource management in modern Web services, yet applying pretrained Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) to downstream tasks remains challenging due to domain shifts. Existing retrieval-augmented approaches typically retrieve coarse-grained window contexts and may introduce context-specific noise. To address this problem, we argue that temporal patterns should be reused at a decomposition level, as effective trend and seasonal dynamics may originate from different contexts. We propose \method, a two-stage \underline{F}ine-grained \underline{K}nowledge \underline{A}ugmentation framework that decouples and consolidates pre-training knowledge into compact, task-shared residual codebooks to enhance frozen TSFMs. Specifically, Stage I constructs dual-branch residual codebooks for decoupled trend and seasonal signals, while Stage II dynamically retrieves and merges these fine-grained patterns into target representations via task-adaptive aggregation and gate fusion. Extensive experiments across eight real-world benchmarks with four representative TSFM backbones demonstrate the superior effectiveness and computational efficiency of \method, while further validating the strong transferability of the residual codebooks across different backbones. The source code is available at the anonymous repository: https://github.com/yuppielqx/TSFM-Component-Token-Adapter

papers.title: Agent-R$^2$: Scaling Agents for Realistic Productivity Work via Real-Source Data Synthesis
papers.abstract_en: Large language models have made rapid progress in agentic reasoning and tool use, raising expectations for agents that can take over realistic productivity work from humans. However, current agents still struggle to finish such tasks, where success requires following long-horizon professional workflows, understanding heterogeneous file contexts, and producing usable deliverables under fine-grained requirements. A key bottleneck is the lack of scalable post-training data that reflects real work intent, authentic file environments, and deliverable-level evaluation. To close this gap, we introduce Agent-R$^2$, a $\textbf{r}$eal-source data synthesis framework that scales training data for $\textbf{r}$ealistic productivity work. Instead of relying on manually specified workflows or LLM-generated files, Agent-R$^2$ grounds synthesis throughout the pipeline in real occupational seeds, corpus-derived workflow evidence, and authentic web-sourced files. From 10k web-corpus candidates, Agent-R$^2$ distills 4k task instances that pair real multi-format attachments with fine-grained, deliverable-level rubrics. On this data, we train Agent-R$^2$-4B via supervised fine-tuning and rubric-based reinforcement learning, improving both end-to-end productivity performance and file-grounded reasoning. Trained on only 4k instances, Agent-R$^2$-4B surpasses Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 on both GDPval (51.0$\%$ vs. 48.0$\%$) and OfficeQA (14.8$\%$ vs. 13.8$\%$). Further analysis shows that Agent-R$^2$ mitigates shortcut behavior, where agents produce superficially plausible deliverables before sufficiently grounding, constructing, or verifying them, while promoting sustained exploration.

papers.title: EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL
papers.abstract_en: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has advanced generative model post-training in verifiable domains such as code and mathematics, but evaluating video quality, especially emotional expression, often depends on subjective aesthetics and has no uniquely correct target. Existing approaches typically rely on fixed rewards for visual quality, motion quality, and text alignment that poorly capture emotional intent and can invite reward hacking, while RLHF is difficult to scale and subject to individual aesthetic differences that complicate the calibration of facial, body motion, and chromatic cues across narrative contexts. We introduce EmoReward, a new self-evolving training mechanism that distills evidence reliability from reward traces collected during an actual training run to adaptively guide multi-reward weight allocation in subsequent training by determining which emotional evidence to trust and how much to weight it. EmoReward first plans specific grounding cues from the emotional prompt to guide evaluation, then uses heterogeneous signal primitives to score the generated video during the act stage. Reflective Reward Gating calibrates their contributions through instance-level gates for phase, face confidence, conflict, and subtlety, then renormalizes weights over the active set to produce the sample's fused reward. RewardMemory then estimates each primitive's reliability from rollout scores and outcomes within each emotional regime in the finished training run, then fixes bounded multipliers that calibrate fusion weights in the next training run without updating reward models. Experiments on HunyuanVideo 1.5 show improvements across multiple RL algorithms and compare EmoReward with other agentic reward methods under SAGE-GRPO. Ablations and transfer experiments on SD 3.5 and FLUX further support adaptive reward calibration for visual generation.

papers.title: Recasting Visual Language Models as EEG Foundation Models for Clinical Neurodiagnostics
papers.abstract_en: Historically automated electroencephalography (EEG) systems was done using task-specific supervised models trained on purposely annotated data. A more recent modeling paradigm relies on creating a unified representation, or a 'foundation model', for multiple modality-specific tasks through large-scale domain-specific pretraining on the unannotated EEG signal. The quality of this unified representation directly depends on the availability of the modality-specific datasets. At the same time, generalist Vision Language Models (VLMs) exhibit broad few-shot learning capacities as well as good fine-tuning adaptability to different visual and language tasks. Can VLMs learn how to read and interpret EEG visually, emulating to a degree the way human clinicians inspect the EEG patterns? In this work we make a case that they can: we show that generalist VLMs without large-scale EEG pretraining perform competitively across a collection of clinical neuro-diagnostic tasks, can adapt to different tasks in a few-shot learning setting better than specialist foundation models, and exhibit better performance with model scaling when modality-specific models fail to exhibit.

papers.title: SPOD: Recovering Suppressed Temporal Evidence in Video-LLMs via Single-Pass Orthogonal Decomposition
papers.abstract_en: Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs) have achieved strong performance on many video understanding tasks, yet remain vulnerable to temporal hallucination in time-sensitive reasoning scenarios such as scene transition understanding and event ordering. Existing solutions either require costly retraining or introduce inefficient multi-pass inference and external supervision at test time. In this work, we show that temporal evidence is already encoded in Video-LLM hidden representations but is not fully exploited during standard inference. Motivated by this observation, we propose Single-Pass Orthogonal Decomposition (SPOD), a training-free framework that recovers suppressed temporal evidence through analytical hidden-state manipulation in a single forward pass. SPOD consists of two components: Frame Distinctiveness Analysis (FDA), which identifies salient frames from middle-layer hidden-state geometry, and Temporal Delta Subspace (TDS), which constructs orthogonal temporal and prior subspaces from weighted inter-frame hidden-state differences. By decomposing final hidden states into temporal, prior, and residual components and rescaling them independently, SPOD enhances dynamic information, suppresses static appearance bias, and preserves complementary information. Experiments on VidHalluc, EventHallusion, and VideoMMMU show that SPOD consistently outperforms strong inference-time baselines across temporal reasoning tasks and model architectures while retaining near-vanilla inference efficiency. These results suggest that improving temporal reasoning in Video-LLMs may depend not only on additional supervision, but also on recovering temporal evidence already present in their internal representations. Our code is available at https://github.com/VioAgnes/SPOD.

papers.title: Where Do Reported Long-Video QA Gains Come From? A Controlled Audit of Frame Selection, Evidence Injection, and Expert Routing
papers.abstract_en: Long-video question answering is usually studied as frame selection: which few frames should a vision-language model see? We introduce VideoRouteAudit, a controlled audit that separates this choice from two alternatives, injecting non-visual evidence and routing to another answering model. It holds the backbone, frame budget, decoding, prompt and grader fixed while varying one decision at a time. On the full Video-MME long bucket (n=900, K=8), no tested selector significantly improves over uniform sampling. The largest selection-only estimate is +1.9 pt (95% CI [-1.2,+5.0]) and our cascade is +1.2 pt [-1.7,+4.1]; all are equivalent to uniform within +/-5 pt. The same contrasts are unstable at the n=200 subset scale commonly used: three of four are up to 3.8x larger, one reverses sign, and resampled 200-item subsets reverse the full-bucket effect's sign in 35.8% of draws. The audit also corrects our own first results. The anomaly-domain "+ASR" arms injected no text, so the pooled +4.7 pt gain was selection plus a development prefix. With transcripts, ASR lowers XD-Violence accuracy by 10.0 pt when appended after the question and not at all when placed before it, and lowers UCF-Crime by 13.0 pt either way; on Video-MME, placing it first adds about 4 pt (7 on Qwen2-VL) to uniform sampling and to the cascade alike (post hoc, unadjusted). Swapping the answering model gives the largest contrast (+15.1 pt on MUSIC-AVQA, +33.3 pt on its worst type), but the same audio-visual expert with its soundtrack silenced keeps 92% of the gain (69% with a mismatched soundtrack), so the contrast is mostly a model swap. Code, per-item predictions and scripts that recompute every statistic are available at https://github.com/mikeslin-ir/long-video-qa-audit.

papers.title: Big Models, Small Gains: Frozen Forecasters as Classifiers on MONSTER
papers.abstract_en: Forecasting foundation models are increasingly used as frozen feature extractors for time series classification, but it remains unclear whether their pretrained representations offer an advantage over strong classifiers that do not require pretraining. This raises an important question: do these representations provide useful information beyond what the model architecture alone can capture, particularly when labelled data are scarce? We present a controlled benchmarking of two forecasting models, Reverso and Chronos-Bolt, on six large datasets from the MONSTER benchmark, using 1%, 10%, and 100% of the available training labels. We compare their frozen representations against four established time series classification methods and random-weight versions of the same forecasting models. Our results show that pretraining improves classification accuracy over random-weight counterparts on five of the six datasets, with gains of up to 23 percentage points. However, the frozen representations do not reliably outperform the strongest non-pretrained baseline in any setting: they perform worse in 15 of 17 settings and tie in the remaining two. Further experiments show that restoring amplitude information recovers part of the performance gap, while fine-tuning and forecast-error features do not close it. These findings highlight the importance of strong task specific baselines and random weight controls when evaluating forecasting foundation models for classification. Our code is available at https://github.com/Rachet2006/frozen-forecasters-monster.

papers.title: SD-LoRA: Training-Time Structural Distillation into LoRA for Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation
papers.abstract_en: Few-shot adaptation of vision-language models must balance two competing goals: learning fine-grained visual distinctions from very limited supervision and preserving the efficiency that makes frozen CLIP-like models attractive for deployment. Existing lightweight adaptation methods, including prompt tuning, LoRA, and cache-based adapters, typically supervise global image embeddings and therefore underuse token-level structure. Conversely, structure-aware methods exploit local evidence but often introduce additional inference-time computation. We propose SD-LoRA, a structural distillation framework that uses token-level graph reasoning only during training and transfers its effects into a lightweight LoRA-adapted CLIP model. During training, a heterogeneous graph teacher models patch-patch, global-local, and visual-text relations over high-resolution ViT tokens. Rather than retaining this graph at test time, SD-LoRA transfers its structural bias into the shared CLIP-LoRA backbone through implicit distillation and Prototype Predictive Alignment, which aligns graph-conditioned representations with support-derived class prototypes. At inference, the graph teacher is discarded; prediction requires only a single CLIP-LoRA forward pass and a cache-based classifier. Across 11 few-shot benchmarks, SD-LoRA improves over a strong CLIP-LoRA baseline by 2.4/1.8/3.0/2.4/2.0 percentage points in the 1/2/4/8/16-shot settings, respectively, without additional graph computation at test time. Results on base-to-novel generalization, cross-dataset transfer, out-of-distribution robustness, and calibration further show that training-time structural supervision improves both accuracy and transfer reliability. Code is available at https://github.com/MR-Sherif/SD-LoRA.git.

papers.title: Server-Side Sparse Assignment for Federated Mixture-of-Experts
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly recognized for their remarkable capabilities; federated learning (FL) offers a promising framework for collaboratively fine-tuning LLMs on edge devices while achieving data privacy. However, edge devices are inherently heterogeneous: clients may exhibit diverse data distributions and resource constraints, including limited memory and computation budgets. Recent federated Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) approaches address these challenges by using sparse expert activation or partial expert loading. However, existing partial-expert methods rely on heuristic full-pool observations or prioritize system-wide load balance, without guarantees for recovering client-specific relevant experts from partial observations. We propose $S^3$-MoE, a server-side sparse expert assignment framework that estimates client-specific expert relevance from partial observations and refines assignments through an exploit--explore mechanism. We also establish relevance-estimation error and exact Top-$K$ recovery guarantees. Experiments using a CNN-based MoE on CIFAR-100 show that $S^3$-MoE recovers task-dependent client--expert preferences and reduces conflicts caused by correlated expert selection across clients. Compared with Full-20 FedAvg, which gives each client access to all 20 experts for local Top-5 routing, $S^3$-MoE achieves 1.31 percentage points higher mean final accuracy while loading only $5$ experts per client.

papers.title: XuanJian-DINOSAR: A SAR Foundation Model Based on Global and Local Semantic Consistency
papers.abstract_en: Self-supervised pre-training on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery enables transferable representations, but the optical-SAR domain gap and speckle perturbations limit representation stability. Most SAR foundation models use masked image modeling (MIM) through pixel reconstruction or structural feature prediction, which is sensitive to speckle or relies on predefined operators. Joint modeling of cross-view semantics and perturbation stability at corresponding spatial locations remains underexplored. We propose XuanJian-DINOSAR, a SAR foundation model based on global and local semantic consistency. We curate over 360K publicly available SAR target chips, detection images, and scene images spanning diverse targets, scenes, and sensors, and adapt an optically pre-trained DINOv2 model to SAR through self-supervised learning. The framework combines DINO global semantic self-distillation, iBOT local masked modeling, and KoLeo feature-distribution regularization to learn globally discriminative and locally structure-aware representations. We introduce a local semantic consistency branch tailored to SAR intensity statistics and coherent imaging characteristics. Shared geometric transformations produce spatially aligned teacher weak views and student strong views. Intensity transformations and Gamma multiplicative speckle perturbations are applied to student views, while a cosine consistency loss aligns patch tokens at corresponding locations, promoting stability under radiometric perturbations. This objective complements the cross-region and cross-scale semantic consistency of DINOv2 multi-crop training, jointly enforcing global and local semantic consistency. Experiments on multiple downstream classification and detection datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on most evaluation metrics, validating the generality and transferability of the learned representations.

papers.title: FedIA: Instance-Aware Cross-Modal Representations for Federated Prompt Learning
papers.abstract_en: Federated Prompt Learning (FPL) enables parameter-efficient adaptation of pre-trained Vision-Language Models across decentralized clients without exchanging raw data. To cope with cross-client heterogeneity, existing FPL methods typically pair a globally shared prompt with a client-specific local prompt. However, this design personalizes only at the client level: the same local prompt is applied to all samples of a client, and the global and local prompts are combined in an input-agnostic, fixed manner. Consequently, it overlooks the substantial visual variations among samples within the same client and cannot adjust the balance between shared and personalized knowledge to each input. To address these limitations, we propose Federated Prompt Learning with Instance-Aware Cross-Modal Representations (FedIA), an FPL framework that learns instance-aware cross-modal representations. Specifically, FedIA first uses global text prompts as client-invariant semantic anchors to select image patches most relevant to each candidate class, suppressing distracting regions. The selected visual evidence then conditions the generation of instance-aware local text representations. Finally, an adaptive global-local fusion module calibrates the contributions of local and global text representations for each image-class pair. In this way, FedIA shifts personalization in FPL from the client level to the instance level while preserving the semantic knowledge shared across clients. Extensive experiments under domain shift, pathological label skew, and Dirichlet-based label skew show that FedIA outperforms FPL baselines, with maximum accuracy gains of 1.44\%-4.37\% over the latest baseline across the three settings. Ablation studies and analyses further verify the complementary contributions of instance-aware representation generation and adaptive global-local fusion.

papers.title: From Tokens to Trajectories: Parameter-Efficient Continuous Adaptation of Unified Multimodal Models
papers.abstract_en: While discrete tokenization in Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) establishes strong semantic reasoning, it introduces a strict quantization bottleneck that degrades fine-grained visual details, often resulting in structurally accurate but artifact-heavy images. We introduce FlowShift, a parameter-efficient post-training framework that bypasses this bottleneck by converting pre-trained discrete UMMs into continuous rectified-flow generators. Instead of discarding the backbone's semantic priors, FlowShift replaces discrete visual interfaces with continuous latent projections and applies LoRA to the attention layers. To efficiently boost visual quality without semantic drift, we propose Dual-Objective Velocity Vector Distillation (DOVD), which aligns the model with a high-fidelity continuous teacher and ground-truth continuous trajectories. This approach drastically improves perceptual quality while preserving prompt adherence and reasoning. When applied to leading discrete UMMs, FlowShift significantly improves COCO-30K FID and aesthetic scores, while retaining over 99.5% of multimodal understanding capabilities. Ablations confirm DOVD drives generation quality. Ultimately, FlowShift achieves high-fidelity continuous generation without sacrificing pre-trained semantic grounding.

papers.title: Resource-Efficient Reinforcement Learning Post-Training through Elastic Expert Parallelism
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning post-training improves the capabilities of large language models, but generating training responses is a major computational bottleneck. In mixture-of-experts models, workers that finish their assigned responses may remain occupied because their experts are still needed by workers processing longer responses. Consequently, approximately one-third of occupied worker time in the baseline occurs after local response generation finishes. Here we present FlexFloor, a system that enables earlier resource release during synchronous response generation while preserving the expert computation required by ongoing responses. FlexFloor jointly adapts response scheduling and the active group of workers. It uses historical response lengths and memory constraints to guide batching and prompt placement, then progressively releases workers while maintaining expert availability and correct communication. Compared with the verl baseline, FlexFloor generates approximately 65.40% more response tokens per unit of occupied computing time and increases response generation throughput by 52.74%, with little observed variation in rollout reward. By making reinforcement learning post-training more efficient, FlexFloor supports faster development and iterative improvement of large language models and AI agents.

papers.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract_en: Large language models are deployed as long-horizon agents that compose diverse tools across MCP services into executable workflows. Existing MCP environment-scaling methods are data-centric: they first synthesize a database and scenario, then derive tools and tasks from them. As a result, tool interfaces may not match real ones, tool compositions are not grounded in execution, and tasks rarely span more than one environment. We propose ToolSpace, a tool-centric framework that reverses this order. ToolSpace mines data, state, and retry dependencies from adjacent calls in execution traces of real MCP services and open agent corpora, using deterministic rules rather than LLM judgment, and clusters the resulting weighted tool-composition graph into environments. Databases are synthesized only for state-mutating environments, while query and stateless tools replay recorded returns. ToolSpace then performs state-aware random walks with rollback and decompiles each chain into a natural-language task with assertion-based checks, keeping only samples that replay successfully from the initial state. Applied to AutomationBench and tau3-Bench Banking, the pipeline produces harder Pro versions on which 7 frontier models drop by up to 38.2 points. Across seven long-horizon tool-use benchmarks, ToolSpace raises Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from 23.0 to 41.0 average score (43.2 with RL) and GLM-5.2 from 44.6 to 56.6, on par with Claude Opus 5. Ablations show that execution-witnessed edges clearly outperform LLM-judged ones, and performance keeps improving with data and environment scale.

papers.title: CLARA: A Cognitively-Driven Clarification Framework for Grounding Ambiguous Requests
papers.abstract_en: Robotics and AI systems are increasingly deploying large vision-language models (LVLMs) to follow high-level instructions, from routine household chores to more complex organizational tasks. Yet, broad directives like "clean the room" or "organize the desk" frequently omit crucial details about user preferences and specific arrangement of objects that influence the desired outcome. Without any further guidance, such models tend to overestimate their grasp of ambiguous instructions and frequently assume they have sufficient understanding despite missing important details. In this paper, we propose CLARA (Conversational cLArification for Robotic Arrangement), a cognitively-driven clarification framework that proactively elicits key information from users, in a similar fashion as humans' clarification seeking behavior. Through targeted questioning, CLARA refines ambiguous requests into structured, detailed instructions describing precisely how objects should be organized or rearranged, according to the user's preferences. These clarifications then guide a diffusion-based image generation pipeline, producing realistic visual renderings of the final, desired scene. This final rendering also serves as a visual confirmation of the system's understanding from the user. Experimental results and user studies demonstrate that CLARA leads to more accurate and consistent outcomes compared to another State-of-the-Art LVLM system, highlighting the importance of interactive clarification for bridging the gap between vague directives and fully grounded task specifications.

papers.title: VIGOR: Visual Gain Ordering for Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Discrete Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal discrete diffusion language models (dLLMs) generate responses through iterative mask prediction and offer a promising alternative to autoregressive large vision-language models. However, they still suffer from hallucination, producing outputs that are plausible under language priors but insufficiently grounded in the image. We argue that hallucination in multimodal dLLMs is not only a token prediction problem, but also a premature commitment problem: during iterative denoising, some masked positions are unmasked too early because their confidence is driven more by language priors than by visual evidence, and these early commitments can bias later generation. To address this issue, we propose Visual Gain Ordering (VIGOR), a training-free and plug-and-play inference strategy that reorders masked positions according to counterfactual visual evidence. At each denoising step, VIGOR compares the confidence of each candidate token under the original image-conditioned pass and an additional visual-ablation pass, and prioritizes positions whose predictions are more strongly supported by the image. Experiments on LLaDA-V and Lumina-DiMOO show that VIGOR consistently reduces hallucination and improves multimodal reasoning performance across benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/THU-BPM/Vigor.

papers.title: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence
papers.abstract_en: We present \textbf{WeLM-Image}, a unified image foundation model that integrates multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis. Designed for single-GPU deployment in WeChat's large-scale consumer applications, the model processes text, reference images, and target latents as one interleaved sequence. A Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone combines shared attention with independent understanding and generation parameters to limit optimization interference. Equipping each path with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) modules provides sparse capacity, with 31.7B stored parameters and approximately 5.4B generation parameters activated per target latent token. A generation-oriented data engine combines a knowledge-grounded visual vocabulary with large-scale visual clustering to balance semantic coverage and editing tasks, while training-time evaluation guides iterative data refinement. Bilingual annotations and verified editing supervision support progressive training up to native 1.5K resolution. We optimize generation and editing separately with rubric- and checklist-based rewards, then consolidate the specialized policies through noise-aware on-policy distillation. In the reported overall comparisons, the 1536-resolution model ranks first among the evaluated open-source models on PRISM-Bench, Qwen-Image-Bench, and UnicBench. MeanFlow-based few-step distillation yields WeLM-Image-Turbo, which generates a $1024\times1024$ image in 4.98\,s on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU using eight guidance-free steps.

papers.title: Annotator-Free Object Detection via Foundation Model Collaboration
papers.abstract_en: Object detection research remains constrained by high annotation costs and the closed-set assumptions of supervised models, limiting scalability to novel categories. We present a target-dataset annotation-free object detection framework that eliminates the need for human labeling on the target dataset by leveraging the complementary strengths of pretrained foundation models, including segmentation and vision-language systems, combined with a self-refining training loop. To further reduce reliance on expensive LVLM queries, we introduce a landmark-based clustering mechanism that amortizes labeling across image clusters, improving label consistency while lowering computational cost. Our method autonomously generates segmentation proposals, assigns semantic labels through multimodal reasoning, and iteratively improves both localization and classification using a lightweight open-set detector. This modular pipeline enables adaptation to completely unseen object classes and domains without any human-provided target-dataset annotations, while maintaining compatibility with existing detection architectures. Evaluations on COCO, LVIS, ODinW-35, and Roboflow-100 demonstrate substantial performance gains over state-of-the-art open-vocabulary and long-tail detection methods, achieving 60.8 AP on COCO and 47.4 AP on LVIS under zero-shot settings. Beyond strong benchmark results, our approach provides a scalable foundation for real-world detection systems in unknown environments, where annotation is infeasible.

papers.title: USI-Brain: Enhancing Underwater Spatial Intelligence via Spatial Data-Driven Vision-Language Modeling
papers.abstract_en: Underwater spatial reasoning depends on object boundaries and geometric cues that are obscured by scattering, color distortion, and low visibility. Existing underwater resources capture these cues through images, annotations, and depth maps, but provide fragmented supervision for vision-language models. We present a spatial data engine that connects visual appearance with object-level geometry through enhancement, 2D and geometry-assisted question generation, and expert filtering. It produces 4.27M QA pairs across five capability groups. We use this corpus to train USI-Brain and introduce an Underwater Prior-guided Rectifier (UPR) that applies gated corrections to visual features. USI-Bench evaluates the resulting capabilities with 6,525 held-out QA pairs. On its 15 task metrics, USI-Brain and USI-Brain + UPR improve over Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct by 5.76 and 7.63 points on average, respectively, using signed differences on 100-point scales. Ablations show that geometry-assisted supervision improves depth and ordering by 4.8 and 6.1 points with UPR disabled, while UPR adds 18.0 points in scene description under matched training data. Both variants use raw images at evaluation. Across NautData, UWBench, and MarineEval, USI-Brain achieves the best or joint-best score on 28 of 32 metrics. Model weights and USI-Bench will be released at https://github.com/SKY-Zhu-91/USI-Brain.

papers.title: Asynchronous Robot Policies
papers.abstract_en: Scaling vision-language foundation models has significantly advanced generalist robot manipulation, but the increased model scale introduces computational latency that degrades real-time physical reactivity. Existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) architectures execute high-level semantic reasoning and action ex- ecution sequentially within the primary control loop, creating a fundamental tension between semantic-reasoning capability and robot agility. To address this, we propose Asynchronous Robot Policy (ARP), an architectural framework that decouples semantic reasoning from low-level action generation using asynchronous processes operating at independent frequencies. In ARP, a high-capacity Vision-Language Model (VLM) asynchronously updates a semantic memory at low fre- quency, while a lightweight Vision-Action Expert, conditioned on this semantic memory, generates robot actions at a much higher control frequency. Such a formulation, enables having a fast perception-action loop without compromising on the semantic capability. To overcome asynchronous memory staleness, ARP trains the vision-action expert on the semantic staleness and execution delay, with temporally mismatched observation across processes. On Franka manipulation tasks, ARP achieves an 18% higher success rate and 20% less time need for execution in quasi-static setups, while 3-5 times baseline performance in dynamic simulation environments. Furthermore, ARP enables operating the VLM at 10 times lower than its nominal frequency with no significant performance loss making it much more efficient than the baseline. These results highlight the architectural advantages of modeling robot policies as asynchronous processes, enabling real-world reactive deployment without sacrificing the scale of foundation models.

papers.title: Accelerating Long-Context Decoding in Large-Scale Hybrid LLMs Without Retraining
papers.abstract_en: The full-attention layers of large language models (LLMs) make every generated token more expensive than the previous one, slowing models down on long-context tasks. Hybrid models reduce this cost by replacing most full-attention layers with linear-attention layers, but the first still dominate decoding at long contexts. We accelerate these remaining layers without any training or weight changes using combined sparse attention: each layer attends to a sliding window of recent tokens, a pinned prefix, and a fixed budget of most relevant tokens in the context. The window size and budget are found on a per-layer basis using a multi-objective search algorithm. Across six hybrid models from three families, from 4B to 397B parameters, the selected configurations preserve their baseline model's accuracy on 21 long-context datasets. Decoding 64k/256k tokens becomes up to 1.26x/2.22x faster on Qwen3.5-4B, 1.20x/2.23x on Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, and 1.16x/2.06x on Ornith-1.0-397B.

papers.title: RI-Prune: Relation and Information Aware Visual Token Pruning for Multi-Image Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have recently been extended to handle multiple input images, but this extension dramatically increases the visual token budget, making visual-token pruning not merely an efficiency option but a practical necessity. Existing visual-token pruning methods, primarily designed for the single-image setting, rely on attention-derived saliency signals to estimate per-token importance. However, this attention-centric design transfers poorly to the multi-image regime: it causes substantial performance degradation on multi-image benchmarks, suffers from strong positional bias, and loses discriminative attention signals as the number of input images increases. To test whether attention-selected tokens are truly important for multi-image reasoning, we conduct two complementary causal probes Leave-One-In and Leave-One-Deletion, which measure token importance by restoring individual tokens to a zeroed visual sequence or removing them from the full sequence. Attention-based pruners provide only marginal gains over random selection, showing that attention is a weak proxy for visual-token importance in multi-image reasoning. Motivated by this gap, we propose Relation and Information Aware Pruning (RI-Prune), a training-free, attention-free pre-decoder selector for multi-image visual token pruning. RI-Prune scores each visual token using a z-normalized combination of three signals computed from projector outputs: query relevance, cross-image correspondence with compact per-image prototypes, and intra image representativeness. By integrating these signals, RI-Prune performs balanced per-image Top-K selection to preserve information across input images. Across multiple multi-image benchmarks and three LVLM backbones, RI-Prune achieves a stronger trade-off between token reduction and task performance than prior pruning methods, particularly under aggressive token budgets.

papers.title: Concertina: Embodying Manipulation and Cognition in One Diffusion Vision-Language Model
papers.abstract_en: Most vision-language-action (VLA) policies decouple manipulation from cognition by bolting an external action mechanism onto a vision-language model (VLM)--either quantizing actions into discrete tokens whose errors bear no stable correspondence to physical displacements, or delegating continuous trajectory generation to a separate action expert whose gradients compete with or are blocked from updating the VLM backbone. We argue that manipulation and cognition should instead be embodied in the same model, shifting from a decoupled VLA to an Embodied Vision-Language Model (eVLM). We introduce Concertina, an eVLM that places continuous trajectory representation, blockwise generation, and physical-coordinate supervision directly on the computation and parameter path of a shared diffusion VLM backbone. Each control timestep is encoded as one continuous latent action token in the backbone hidden space, and the shared Transformer reconstructs temporally ordered action blocks via the same corrupt-and-reconstruct operator used for multimodal pretraining. Active action projections account for only 0.21% of parameters in the 4.46B model with zero separate action-generator layers, compared with 16.5%-35.1% dedicated action-expert capacity in representative continuous VLAs. Using our proposed Action Interface Audit, we confirm that cross-time trajectory coupling emerges in the middle and late layers of the shared backbone rather than at the action interfaces. On standard benchmarks, Concertina achieves 98.15% average success on regular LIBERO, 85.9% on the 10,030-task LIBERO-Plus benchmark, and 4.142 average completed chain length on CALVIN ABC-D. papers.title: Batch-Conditioned Semantic Anchors for Robust Transductive Adaptation of Vision--Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Transductive adaptation improves vision-language models at test time by refining predictions on an unlabeled batch, but current methods face a key trade-off. Aggressive approaches exploit batch structure but can drift when batches are sparse, have prior shift, or cover little of the label space. Conservative methods better preserve CLIP text semantics, but fixed semantic references can under-adapt even when the batch provides strong corrective evidence. We propose JPTA (Joint Prior and Transport Adaptation), a prior-aware framework that casts transductive VLM adaptation as batch-conditioned semantic reference estimation. Instead of treating CLIP text prototypes as fixed priors or freely replaceable, JPTA views them as semantic references that shift toward image-side batch structure only under calibrated evidence. It estimates batch priors and soft image-side prototypes to form transported semantic references whose impact is scaled by batch reliability. Across standard benchmarks, low effective-class regimes, all-class evaluation, and online streams, JPTA consistently outperforms TransCLIP and StatA, with the largest gains on sparse and prior-shifted batches. Anchor-drift, active-support, and absent-class-mass diagnostics show that JPTA fixes effective-class mismatch without unconstrained transductive drift, indicating that robust transductive VLM adaptation should recalibrate semantic references using reliable batch evidence rather than choose between unrestricted transduction and fixed prototypes. Code is available at https://github.com/MR-Sherif/JPTA.git.

papers.title: Editing Large Language Models with Geometry-Aware Regularization
papers.abstract_en: Knowledge editing has become a key technique for updating knowledge in large language models. However, existing methods neglect the geometric structure of the knowledge representation space, leading to two key limitations: they cannot distinguish which pre-trained knowledge should be preferentially preserved (core vs. non-core) nor which new edits are inherently difficult (hard vs. easy). To address this, we propose GEdit, a geometry-aware framework built on a Low-Rank Plus Diagonal (LR+D) factor model that captures the intrinsic low-rank structure of Transformer FFN hidden representations. GEdit features two complementary mechanisms. First, the low-rank regularization applies targeted protection on a low-rank core knowledge subspace. Second, the adaptive regularization dynamically adjusts the regularization strength based on each edit request's editability: relaxing constraints for hard edits to ensure success, and tightening them for easy edits to better preserve pretrained knowledge. Extensive experiments on GPT2-XL, GPT-J, and LLaMA-3-8B under large-scale editing scenarios, including both mini-batch and fully sequential editing settings with up to 10,000 continuous updates, show that GEdit consistently and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both editing success and knowledge preservation.
